Package io.openlineage.client.utils

Class FabricWarehouseUtils

java.lang.Object
io.openlineage.client.utils.FabricWarehouseUtils
public final class FabricWarehouseUtils extends Object
How OpenLineage names tables in Microsoft Fabric warehouses.

Each Fabric workspace has one SQL address that all its warehouses share, for example 6obaxtbopqfublwdicr5oicqlm-ac4ezc2eudhehd3wgnlpocnuna.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com. A table is named fabric-warehouse://<address> plus <warehouse>.<schema>.<table>.

Some of what this class relies on isn't documented by Microsoft: how the address is built from the tenant and workspace IDs, and the option names that Microsoft's Spark connector for Fabric uses. All of it is kept in this class, and the tests check it against addresses taken from real workspaces, so a change on Microsoft's side only needs fixing here.

  • Method Details

    • canonicalEndpoint

      public static String canonicalEndpoint(String endpoint)
      Normalizes a Fabric address, so the same table always gets the same name.

      The address is lowercased, the .z<two characters> label that Fabric sometimes adds before .datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com is removed, and port 1433, the default, is removed. Any other port is kept as :port.

      Parameters:
      endpoint - host, host:port or host,port
      Returns:
      the normalized address, or just lowercased if it can't be read

    • isFabricEndpoint

      public static boolean isFabricEndpoint(String endpoint)
      Whether this is the SQL address of a Fabric workspace, optionally followed by a numeric port. Addresses used to reach a workspace in another organization have an extra part and aren't matched.

    • endpointFor

      public static String endpointFor(UUID tenantId, UUID workspaceId)
      Builds a workspace's SQL address from its tenant ID and workspace ID. This is needed when only the IDs are known, as with writes from Microsoft's Spark connector for Fabric.

      The address is <tenant part>-<workspace part>.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com. Each part is the ID turned into 26 characters:

      1. take the ID's 16 bytes in the order Microsoft's .NET stores them, which reverses the bytes within each of the first three groups of the ID;
      2. write those bytes in base32 (letters a-z and digits 2-7), lowercase, without trailing = padding.

      For example, tenant cc0b82f3-7c2e-400b-aec3-40a3d720505b and workspace 8b4cb800-a044-43ce-8f76-3356f709b468 give 6obaxtbopqfublwdicr5oicqlm-ac4ezc2eudhehd3wgnlpocnuna.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com.

      Microsoft doesn't document this. In November 2026 it matched the real addresses of 2 test workspaces and 44 public tenants, and Microsoft's own fabric-warehouse-labs samples build the address the same way. If Microsoft changes it, update this method and the known examples in FabricWarehouseUtilsTest. Users can also set the address themselves; see the Spark integration's Microsoft Fabric docs.

    • oneLakeLocation

      public static DatasetIdentifier oneLakeLocation(UUID workspaceId, UUID warehouseId, String schema, String table)
      Builds the location of a table's files in OneLake, Fabric's storage. The path always uses IDs, never names, because OneLake refuses paths that mix the two (error 400 FriendlyNameSupportDisabled).
      Returns:
      namespace abfss://<workspace ID>@onelake.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com and name <warehouse ID>/Tables/<schema>/<table>

    • withOneLakeLocation

      public static DatasetIdentifier withOneLakeLocation(DatasetIdentifier identifier, Optional<String> idWarehouse, Optional<String> workspaceIdOption, Optional<String> warehouseIdOption)
      Adds the table's OneLake file location to a Fabric warehouse dataset, as a LOCATION symlink.

      This needs the warehouse's ID, which is only available when the user passes it with the connector's DatawarehouseId option. That ID belongs to one warehouse, but a query can read tables from several warehouses in the same workspace. So the location is only added to tables in the warehouse the ID was given for; other tables would get a wrong path.

      If anything is missing, the table is in another warehouse, or an ID isn't valid, the dataset is returned as it was.

      Parameters:
      identifier - a fabric-warehouse dataset named <warehouse>.<schema>.<table>
      idWarehouse - name of the warehouse that warehouseIdOption belongs to
      workspaceIdOption - the WorkspaceId option; if not set, the workspace ID is read from the address
      warehouseIdOption - the DatawarehouseId option
      Returns:
      the same dataset, with the location added when possible
